package_info.package_name: Multiple typosquatted packages (e.g., selenim, sleenium, etc.)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages are typosquatted clones of popular Python libraries, containing obfuscated code that, upon installation, deploys a malicious browser extension. This extension manipulates the clipboard to replace copied cryptocurrency wallet addresses with attacker-controlled addresses, enabling theft of cryptocurrency.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the obfuscated Python code executes, extracting and deploying a malicious browser extension to %APPDATA%\Extension.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscated code in setup.py is highly unusual and designed to evade detection. The code performs actions unrelated to package installation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: setup.py should only define package metadata and installation logic, not deploy browser extensions or manipulate the filesystem outside the package scope.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation may be used for commercial software protection, but never in open-source package installers.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After installation, the manifest.json file requests clipboard access permissions for the malicious browser extension.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Requesting clipboard access is a red flag, especially for an unlisted extension installed outside official channels.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate extensions are installed via browser marketplaces and request permissions transparently.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Clipboard access is legitimate for password managers or productivity tools, but not for hidden extensions.
key_indicators: Manifest file deployed outside normal browser extension paths

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the background.js script monitors clipboard events and replaces any detected cryptocurrency wallet address with a hardcoded attacker-controlled address.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and modifying clipboard data to replace crypto addresses is a classic 'clipper' malware technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Browser extensions should not silently alter clipboard data, especially to redirect funds.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Clipboard monitoring may be used for accessibility tools, but not for silent data replacement.
key_indicators: Regular expressions for crypto wallet patterns

execution_context.file_location: Windows browser shortcut files (e.g., C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu, %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu, %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Internet Explorer\Quick Launch\User Pinned\TaskBar)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code modifies browser shortcut files to force browsers to load the malicious extension on startup.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Modifying browser shortcuts to load unlisted extensions is a stealthy persistence technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Installers should not alter unrelated application shortcuts or force browser extension loading.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise deployments may pre-load extensions, but with user/admin consent.
key_indicators: Targeting multiple browsers (Chrome, Edge, Opera, Brave)

attack_chain.action: User installs a typosquatted malicious package from PyPI.
Obfuscated setup.py code executes, deploying a malicious browser extension to %APPDATA%\Extension.
attack_chain.leads_to: Browser extension files written to disk

attack_chain.action: Installer modifies browser shortcut files to force browsers to load the malicious extension.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious extension loaded on browser startup

attack_chain.action: Malicious extension requests clipboard permissions and monitors clipboard events.
When a crypto wallet address is copied, the extension replaces it with an attacker-controlled address.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated code in setup.py or other installer scripts
Installer writes files to %APPDATA%\Extension or similar non-standard extension paths
Modification of browser shortcut files to inject --load-extension argument
Browser extension requesting clipboard permissions and containing regexes for crypto wallet addresses
Clipboard content replaced with hardcoded wallet addresses
file_indicators: Browser shortcut files modified to include --load-extension
network_indicators: N/A (primary attack is local clipboard manipulation, but exfiltration or update C2 may be present in some variants)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for obfuscated or suspicious code in setup.py during package installation. Detect creation of unauthorized browser extension directories in user profiles, especially %APPDATA%\Extension. Alert on modifications to browser shortcut files that add --load-extension arguments. Scan browser extensions for clipboard permissions and regex patterns matching cryptocurrency wallet addresses. Monitor clipboard events for unauthorized replacement of wallet addresses.
